audit_findings.title: The null perimeter misses a completed transformation of Conifer
audit_findings.magnitude: $1.900 billion aggregate consideration; $540 million offset; $1.242 billion carrying value of the remaining CHI note at 2026-06-30; $826 million contract-termination revenue recognized in the first half of 2026
audit_findings.mechanism: Changes recurring OE through full Conifer ownership and the termination of CHI revenue, while the settlement note and receipts require separate bridge treatment.
audit_findings.evidence: Subject to the terms of that agreement and other related contracts, the parties have agreed to, among other things: (1) terminate the RCM Agreement effective as of December 31, 2026; (2) CHI’s payment to us of an aggregate amount equal to $1.900 billion in annual installments over the next three years; provided that, of such amount, $540 million was satisfied on January 27, 2026 by offsetting the $540 million due to CHI from Conifer as described in the next clause; and (3) the reduction of our redeemable noncontrolling interest balance, and an increase in our additional paid-in capital balance associated with the redemption by Conifer of CHI’s minority equity interest in Conifer, in exchange for a payment by Conifer of $540 million, which redemption is effective as of January 1, 2026.
audit_findings.explanation: This is a demonstrated perimeter error, not merely a possibility. The forecast begins after Tenet obtained 100% of Conifer and agreed to end a major customer contract, yet the valuation uses the pre-transaction 2025 OE perimeter and a null perimeter adjustment. Direction is mixed: greater ownership and the settlement asset add value, while lost CHI economics and any nonrecurring termination income reduce normalized OE.
audit_findings.action: Rebuild Conifer's parent-attributable OE for 2026 and post-2026, exclude the $826 million termination revenue from recurring OE, and add the CHI note or receipts to the bridge exactly once after reconciling the $540 million offset.

audit_findings.title: Parent earnings are mixed with consolidated cash-flow adjustments
audit_findings.magnitude: 2025 NCI income $960 million, consolidated D&A $863 million and consolidated capital expenditures $1.010 billion; parent-attributable adjustment unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Directly changes the OE numerator by combining parent-attributable net income with depreciation, capital needs and other adjustments that include minority-owned operations.
audit_findings.evidence: For consolidated subsidiaries, our financial statements reflect 100% of the revenues and expenses of the subsidiaries.
audit_findings.explanation: The claim-basis mismatch is demonstrated. The $960 million of 2025 income assigned to NCI is 68% of the $1.407 billion earned by Tenet common shareholders, so consolidated adjustments can be material relative to the $1.114 billion OE anchor. Adding minority-attributable D&A overstates OE, while subtracting minority-attributable capital needs understates it; the net direction cannot be established without allocation data.
audit_findings.action: Allocate 2025 D&A, required capital spending, working-capital movements and every other OE adjustment between Tenet and NCI at the facility level, then rerun the anchor and all scenarios using only parent-attributable amounts.

audit_findings.title: Redeemable NCI creates a material unmodeled claim on parent cash
audit_findings.magnitude: $2.143 billion redeemable NCI at 2026-06-30, including $2.096 billion in Ambulatory Care; $558 million of NCI purchases paid in the first half of 2026
audit_findings.mechanism: Potential redemption payments consume parent cash or financing capacity, while completed purchases also transfer additional subsidiary earnings to the parent and therefore affect both OE and the equity bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: Certain of our investees’ partnership and operating agreements contain terms that, upon the occurrence of specified events, could obligate us to purchase some or all of the noncontrolling interests related to our consolidated subsidiaries.
audit_findings.explanation: The put-related claim and recent cash outflows are demonstrated, although the $2.143 billion carrying amount is not itself a filed maximum cash obligation. Its scale is about 12% of the $17.826 billion base equity value, so it is reasonably capable of changing valuation materially. Direction remains unknown because the model omits both possible purchase payments and the incremental earnings acquired in exchange.
audit_findings.action: Inventory each remaining redemption right, obtain exercise dates and pricing formulas, estimate maximum and expected cash payments, and rerun OE and the bridge with both the payment and acquired parent-attributable earnings modeled consistently.

audit_findings.title: The bridge may treat non-distributable consolidated cash as parent excess cash
audit_findings.magnitude: $2.170 billion added to the bridge, equal to $25.56 per diluted share; $86 million was identified as intended for insurance-related subsidiaries, while the remaining unavailable portion is unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Reduces the cash/STI bridge addition to the extent consolidated cash is partner-owned, restricted, insurance-dedicated or required for normal operations.
audit_findings.evidence: Subsidiaries that are not wholly owned may also be subject to restrictions on their ability to distribute cash to us in their financing or other agreements and, as a result, we may not be able to access their cash flows to service their respective debt obligations.
audit_findings.explanation: Adding the full consolidated balance as excess parent cash is demonstrated, but the record does not establish how much is actually unavailable. The specifically identified $86 million equals about $1.01 per share and only 0.5% of base equity value; that amount alone is not material, while a materially larger restricted or operating-cash requirement remains possible but unquantified.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile cash by legal entity, ownership and restriction; document captive-insurance and minimum operating-liquidity requirements; then rerun the bridge using only cash distributable to Tenet common shareholders.

audit_findings.title: Projected growth may require acquisition and partner-buyout spending excluded from OE
audit_findings.magnitude: $300 million of 2025 Ambulatory Care revenue growth came from acquisitions, de novo development and control purchases; related 2025 cash investment was $339 million and first-half 2026 investment was $144 million
audit_findings.mechanism: Reduces forecast OE when acquisition, de novo and partner-buyout spending is necessary to produce the growth embedded in the base or bull scenarios.
audit_findings.evidence: The change was driven by (1) a $300 million increase from 2024 and 2025 acquisitions, de novo development and purchases of controlling interests, partially offset by the impact of the sale or closure of certain facilities, and (2) a $338 million increase in same‑facility net operating revenues, which was primarily attributable to incremental revenue from negotiated commercial rate increases, higher patient acuity and the addition of new service lines during 2025.
audit_findings.explanation: The historical reliance on external investment is demonstrated, although the future spending required for 3% or 6% growth is not yet quantified. Recent annual investment equals roughly 30% of the $1.114 billion OE anchor, making the omission reasonably capable of materially overstating forecast distributable cash if scenario growth assumes continued roll-up activity.
audit_findings.action: Separate organic parent-attributable OE growth from acquired growth, determine the all-in recurring investment needed for each scenario, and rerun base and bull cases after deducting that spending or lowering growth to an organic rate.

audit_findings.title: Mandatory California seismic spending is absent from the steady-state forecast
audit_findings.mechanism: Future mandatory compliance capital expenditures would reduce OE during the explicit forecast period through 2030.
audit_findings.evidence: At this time, we are unable to estimate the cost of this work.
audit_findings.explanation: The compliance obligation and deadline are established, but Tenet states that the cost cannot yet be estimated because final facility designs, regulatory review and scope remain outstanding. It is therefore a forward-looking exposure not presently measurable in the filed numbers, rather than a quantified current valuation error.
audit_findings.action: Obtain facility-level SPC and NPC budgets and construction schedules after state review, compare them with the maintenance-capital allowance, and rerun forecast OE for any incremental spending once estimates become available.

audit_findings.title: Unidentified D&A is conservatively left in owner earnings
audit_findings.magnitude: $850 million of FY2016 D&A remained expensed; computed effect on the selected 2025 anchor is $0
audit_findings.mechanism: Could increase historical OE if filed evidence later identifies residual D&A as an eligible non-economic add-back, but FY2016 does not enter the selected latest-actual anchor.
audit_findings.evidence: identified eligible D&A is below the filed composite; residual is conservatively left as an expense, not added back: FY2016 $850.0m (100.0% of filed D&A)
audit_findings.explanation: The supplied quantified residual relates to 2016. The valuation explicitly rejected the historical trend and anchored solely to 2025 OE of $1.114 billion, so reclassifying the cited $850 million would change the displayed 2016 history but not the anchor, scenario values or buy-below price. No current-year eligible residual has been demonstrated.
audit_findings.action: No valuation rerun is required for the cited FY2016 amount; classify 2025 residual D&A and rerun only if filed evidence establishes an eligible 2025 add-back.
